study_guide.title: Cane and the Falling Sky

pages.text: Cane the Weather Dog looked up at a big gray cloud. "Something is going to fall from the sky today," he said. "When water falls from a cloud, it has a special name — precipitation!" "Precipitation," said Cane, "is any water that falls from the sky. And guess what? It comes in four different kinds. Let's meet them all!"
Cane held out a paw and a drop landed on it. "The first one you know well — rain! Rain is liquid water drops. Rain falls when the air is warm."
pages.ask: Can you wiggle your fingers down like falling rain? Pitter-patter!

pages.text: Then Cane pointed to a cold, snowy day. "When the air is very cold, the water freezes into soft, fluffy ice crystals — snow! And here's a secret: every snowflake has six sides."
pages.ask: Can you show six fingers, like the six sides of a snowflake?

pages.text: "Sometimes," said Cane, "snow melts a little, then re-freezes on the way down into tiny icy pellets. That's called sleet. It goes tap-tap-tap on the window!" "And in big summer storms," Cane went on, "the wind tosses raindrops up high where they freeze into little balls of ice — hail! Hail can even bounce when it lands." "Rain, snow, sleet, and hail," said Cane. "Four kinds of precipitation. And here's the big secret — the temperature decides which one falls. Warm air makes rain. Cold air makes snow!" "Remember the water cycle?" Cane wagged his tail. "Precipitation is the 'falling down' part. The water goes up, makes clouds, and falls back to us — watering the whole Earth!" Then Cane looked serious for a moment. "When it's wet or icy, the ground gets slippery. So we always walk, don't run. And in heavy rain, we stay away from flooded water — Turn Around, Don't Drown."
The rain slowed, and a puddle sparkled at Cane's feet. He gave a happy splash. "Great job, weather watcher," said Cane. "You met all four kinds of precipitation. You are weather-ready!"

study_guide.rule: Precipitation is water falling from clouds — rain, snow, sleet, or hail — and temperature decides which one.

cards.def: hard ice balls from big storms
water falling as rain, snow, sleet, or hail
soft white frozen flakes that fall from clouds

choices: any water that falls from clouds
